Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 12pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be summarized
by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City Council and will
also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be recorded for
public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials
During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members

(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

 GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

  8
 SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

PURPOSE:  Consideration  of  Conditional  Use  Permit  (CUP)  No.  23-0040  to  allow  live
entertainment,  i.e. D.J. and 5-person  band, within  a proposed  banquet  hall ("1951")  located  at 9849
Atlantic  Avenue,  Unit  H. Pursuant  to Table  11.51-1  (Application  and Review  Authority)  of the
South  Gate Municipal  Code Section  11.51.030,  live entertainment  permit  applications  are subject
to review  and approval  by the City  Council.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  the  live  entertainment  permit  for  the  1951  Banquet  Hall  to  have  live
  entertainment  at 9849  Atlantic  Avenue,  Unit  H ("Project  Site")  subject  to the conditions
  set forth  in the permits  and any limitations  and/or  conditions  the City  Council  may wish  to
  impose.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  $200 for the Live  Entertainment  Permit.  Fees will  be collected  annually  upon
the operator's  renewal  of their business  license.

PUBLIC  NOTIFICATION:  Advertising  and notification  of the public  hearing  was conducted  in
compliance  with  Chapter  11.50.020,  of the South Gate Municipal  Code. Notice  of the hearing  was
originally  posted  and priblished  in the "South  Gate Press"  newspaper  and was mailed  to the
surrounding  properties  on June 25, 2024.

ENVIRONMENTAL  ELEVATION:  The City  of South  Gate has determined  that the proposed
project  qualifies  for a categorical  exemption  under  CEQA  Guidelines  Section  15301,  (Class  1)
"Existing  Facilities",  in that the project  involves  a negligible  expansion  of (live  entertainment)
activities  allowed  witin  a banquet  hall without  alterations  or expansion  to an existing  commercial
building,  and thereby  is exempt  from  CEQA.

BACKGROUND:  On  April  16,  2023,  during  a regularly  scheduled  Planning  Commission
meeting,  the Planning  Comtnission  approved  a request  for a Conditional  Use Permit  (CUP)  No.
23-0030  to allow  the catering  of alcoholic  beverages  (ABC  license  Type  58) in conjunction  with
a banquet  hall;  and on-site  consumption  of beer and wine  (ABC  license  Type  41) in conjunction
with  a full-service  breakfast  restarirant,  The Pan.

 In addition,  live  entertainment  was proposed  as part of the project.  However,  pursuant  to Table
11.51-1  of the  South  Gate  Municipal  Code  (SGMC)  Section  11.51.030  (Review  types  and
responsibilities),  the City  Council  is designated  as the review  arithority  for final  approval  of a Live
Entertainment  Permit.  As a result,  the Planning  Commission  approved  the project  without  live
entertainment.

As  part  of  the  project,  the  Community  Development  Director  approved  an Administrative
Modification,  granting  a ten percent  (10%)  reduction  in the mimber  of off-street  parking  spaces
required  by the Zoning  Code  based  on the existing  rises within  the subject  site, resulting  in a
reduction  of 11 off-street  parking  spaces. The Project  Site is developed  with  94 parking  spaces.
With  the approval  of the Administrative  Modification,  the project  is required  to provide  a total  of
93 parking  spaces, thus making  the Project  compliant  with parking  reqriirements.

On April  18, 2023, the Department  of Community  Development  received  an application  from Liliger
Damaso,  Applicant,  for Conditional  Use Permit  to allow  the operation  of a banquet  hall with  live
entertainment;  to cater alcoholic  beverages  with a Type 58 ABC  license; the sale of beer and wine for
on-site  consumption  with  a type  41 ABC  license;  and a full-service  breakfast  restaurant  at 9849
Atlantic  Ave, Units H and I

ANALYSIS:  The Project  Site is located  within  an existing  shopping  center at the northwest  corner
of Tweedy  Boulevard  and Atlantic  Avertue.  There  is an existing  22-foot-tall  solid  masong  wall
located  along  the westerly  and northerly  boundaries  of the subject  site, between  the shopping
center  and adjacent  residentials  uses. The shopping  center consists  of two buildings.  A restaurant
pad ("El  Pescador")  is located  at the easterly  portion  of the site, fronting  Atlantic  Avetue.  The
other  commercial  building  is situated  along  the north  and westerly  edges of the site and hosts a
variety  of businesses,  including  the banquet  hall  and breakfast  restaurant.  The proposed  banquet
hall and restaurant  will  be in suites H and I, respectively,  and share a cooking  facility.  There  are a
total of 94 parking  spaces throughout  the shopping  center.  The banquet  hall will  have operational
horirs  from  5:00 pm to 12:00  am, Monday  through  Sunday.  Live  entertainment  in the form  of DJ
or 5-person  band  will  be playing  during  the horirs  of operation.  The banquet  hall  will  have  a
maximum  capacity  of 171 people.  The applicant  anticipates  having  five (5) employees  and one (1)
security  guard  on staff  during  the banquet  hall's  horirs  of operation.  The restaurant's  hours  of
operation  will  be from  8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.,  Monday  through  Sunday.

In anticipation  of the potential  noise generated  by the proposed  live entertainment.  The applicant
hired  Innovative  Noise  Consulting  to conduct  a Noise  Impact  Study  at the Project  Site. A study
was conducted  at 6:00 pm and 7:00 pm on a Friday  evening.  The study  was conducted  to predict
constant  steady-state  noise levels  at the banquet  hall and within  the surrounding  environment.  The
results  were based on the loudest  (allowable)  operating  noise levels,  which  showed  that the sound
pressure  in the surrounding  residential  area will  be at most  39. This  noise  level  is within  the
allowed  nighttime  noise level limit  of 40. The applicant  will  install  a hardware  or software  volume
limiter  to ensure that the noise level  is below  the permitted  noise level  during  hours  of operation
and is conditioned  to mitigate  any potential  noise pollution  exceeding  the City's  Maxitum  sound
levels  per Section  11.34.080  of SGMC.

Basedonthe  comprehensiveNoise  Impact  Study,  existing  site conditions,  andproposedmitigation
measures,  including  a volume  limited  to ensure  compliance  with  noise regulations,  the proposed

3. Noise  Fundamentals

Noise  is defined  as unwanted  sound.  Noise  can be generated  by man-made  sources,  for example  traffic
and  construdion,  or natural  sources  such as thunder  and wildlife  calls.  Excessive  noise  has the  potential  to
cause  negative  effects  on  humans  including  speech  interFerence,  hearing  damage,  emotional  and
behavioral  stress,  sleep  deprivation  as well  as increased  blood  pressure  and heart  rate.  As well  as humans,
excess  noise  can  negatively  affect  animals  by potentially  leading  to habitat  relocation  or loss of habitat,
behavioral  stress,  communication  interFerence,  hearing  loss and  lower  reproduction  rates.  The  following
subsections  present  the  fundamental  concepts  used  commonly  in noise  analyses.

  3.I  Sound  Pressure  Levels and the Decibel  Scale
Sound  is generated  by pressure  waves  in air that  are perceived  by the  human  ear as our sense  of hearing.
Changes  in air pressure  can be used  to measure  sound,  however  these  air pressure  changes  can vary,  most

commonly, in orders of magnitude from 20 micropascals (4Pa) to 200 pascals (Pa).As a more convenient
method  to  measure  sound  pressure  levels  and  reduce  the  need  to  analyze  values  in several  orders  of
magnitude,  these  numbers  are converted  to a logarithmic  scale  known  as the Decibel  Scale (dB). Examples
of common  sound  levels  are shown  in Figure  3-A.

  3.2 Frequency  and the A-weighting  Scale
The character  of sound  can often  be described  as low pitch  such as a hum, high pitch  such as a shriek  or
a mixture  of low and high sounds.  Scientifically,  this perception  can be described  in terms  of frequency.
Frequency  is measured  in Hertz  (Hz) and is defined  as the number  of wave cycles  per second.  A healthy,
young  human  ear is capable  of hearing  frequencies  between  20 Hertz  to 20,000  Hertz.  Low frequency
sounds  such  as naturally  occurring  ocean  waves  or the  sound  output  of subwoofers,  propagate  more
efficiently  though  air than higher  frequency  sounds.  This is why at distance,  these sources  of sound  can be
heard  as a low rumble  but up close,  higher  frequencies  are audible.

As the  human  ear is not  equally  sensitive  to sound  levels  within  the  audible  frequency  spectrum  (20-
20kHertz),  the A-weighting  scale  is often  applied  to measured  sound  levels.  The A-weighting  scale was
developed  to approximate  the frequency  sensitivity  of the human  ear. At frequencies  up to approximately
1,000  Hertz, the A-weighting  scale reduces  the sound  levels in comparison  to the unweighted  equivalent.
At  frequencies  between  approximately  1,000  Hertz  and  5,000  Hertz,  where  the  human  ear  is more
sensitive,  the A-weighting  scale increases  the otherwise  unweighted  sound  levels.  At frequencies  below
1,000  Hertz,  where  the  human  ear  is  less  sensitive,  the  A-weighting  scale  decreases  the
otherwise  unweighted  sound  levels.  When  the A-weighting  scale has been  applied  to a decibel  level, the
unit of measurement  is often  shown  as dBA or dB(A).  The graph  in Figure  3-B shows  the constants  that
can be applied  to the unweighted  scale to calculate  a sound  level in the A-weighting  scale.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION  DECLARING  A  CONTINUED  EMERGENCY  AND
AUTHORIZING  REPAIR,  REPLACEMENT  OR  MAINTENANCE  ACTIVITIES  OF
PUBLIC  FACILITIES  RELATED  TO  THE  URBAN  ORCHARD,  CITY  PROJECT  NO.
539-PRK  WITHOUT  PUBLIC  BIDDING,  PURSUANT  TO  THE  EMERGENCY
CONTRACTING  PROCEDURES  OF THE SOUTH  GATE  MUNICIPAL  CODE  AND
THE CALIFORNIA  PUBLIC CONTRACT  CODE

PURPOSE:  To declare  an emergency  still  exists and to authorize  the repair,  replacement  or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard  Project  without  public
bidding.  The  Los  Angeles  County  Department  of  Public  Health,  Solid  Waste  Division
("County")  issued a Corrective  Action  Order requiring  construction  to stop on the project.  The
declaration  of  emergency  is necessary  to streamline  the process  to procure  a replacement
contractor to provide maintenance  activities to preserve the site in a safe condition  until  the
County authorizes construction work on the project to resume.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider  making  a finding  and adopting
a Resolution  declaring  an emergency  still  exists  and  authorizing  repair,  replacement  or
maintenance  activities  of public  facilities  related  to the Urban  Orchard,  City  Project  No.  539-
PRK, without public bidding, pursuant to the emergency contracting  procedures  of the South
Gate Municipal Code and the California Public Contract Code.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The  Urban  Orchard  Project
("Project")  has received a total of $30.5 million in grant and other funds for design, construction,
operations,  and maintenance, as summarized below.

ANALYSIS:
The Project  was under  construction  and approximately  90%  of construction  work  has been
completed.  On December  29, 2022, the City received  a Corrective  Action  Order ("Order")  from
the County.  The Order required  the City to stop all construction  activities  until  such a time as a
Post Closure  Land Use Plan ("PCLUP")  for the Project  site was approved  by the County.  Given
the PCLUP approval process and input  received  to date, it will  take at least several months,
possibly six or more, to obtain approval.

 To  avoid  the  significant  delay  damages  that  would  be payable  by  the  City  to the  general
contractor  during  a prolonged  suspension  of the project  pending  approval  of the PCLUP,  the City
Council  ten'ninated  the general  contractor's  agreement  at a Special  City  Council  meeting  on
February  6, 2023.  Such teri'nination  provided  both  iini'nediate  and long-teim  cost savings  to the
City  but also created  an immediate  need for the City  to retain  an interim  contractor  to perfoim
certain  ongoing  maintenance  and safety  activities;  a need wliich  must  be met  sooner  than  the
time necessary  to engage in normal  public  bidding  procedures

The proposed  Resolution  declares  a continued  emergency  exists pursuant  to the authority  granted
by South  Gate Municipal  Code  § 1.54.470  and California  Public  Contract  Code  § 22050.  Those
Code  Sections  allow  cities,  by resolution,  to approve  the City's  entry  into  contracts  without
engaging  in public  bidding  where  certain  emergency  conditions  are found  to have occurred.  Staff
continues  to believe  that the County's  Order  directing  all construction  work  to be ceased on the
Project,  constitutes  such an emergency  due to tlie public's  safety  witli  an unfinished  construction
site and the need to respond  accordingly  to additional  directives  given  by the County  related  to
ensuring  public  safety.  Staff  are recoinmending  that  the  City  Council  adopt  the  proposed
Resolution  so that the City  can avail  itself  of the accelerated  contracting  procedures  authorized
by those  Code  Sections.  The  Resolution,  (1)  declares  an emergency,  (2)  authorizes  the City
Manager  to take  such  actions  deemed  necessary  to  cause  the  maintenance  activities  to be
perfon'ned  and to procure  the necessary  equipment,  services,  and supplies  all without  giving
notice  for bids for contracts,  (3) requires  that at each regularly  sclieduled  City  Council  Meeting,
the City  Manager  present  to the  Council  the reasons  justifying  why  the emergency  will  not
pen'nit  a delay  resulting  from  a competitive  solicitation  for bids,  why  that action  is necessary  to
respond  to the emergency,  and that the City  Council  review  the emergency  action  to determine,
by a four-fifth's  vote,  that there is a need to continue  the emergency  action  until  the emergency
action  is terminated.

The  City  is working  diligently  to secure  the PCLUP  approval.  Since  the original  Resolution
declaring  an emergency  was approved  by the City  Council  on February  6, 2023,  the following
contracts,  expenditures,  and milestones  have been undertaken:

  or  maintenance  activities,  with  the  exception  of  those  required  in  the  settlement
  agreement.

  2.  Approved  a funding  increase  for TPL  in the amount  of $50,000.  On January  24, 2023,

BACKGROUND:  The Project  is a part of the FY 2022/23  Capital  Ii'nprovement  Program.  The
Project  is located  between  the Los  Angeles  River,  Firestone  Boulevard,  the Thunderbird  Villa
Mobile  Home  Park, and the I-710  Freeway.  The two primary  purposes  of the Project  are to divert

iiverfront  recreational  opportunities.

The Project  is being  constructed  on a property  that was used as an unpermitted  landfill  until  1949
by an entity  known  as Southeastern  Disposal  and By-Products.  Tlie property  site is identified  in
CalRecycle's  Solid  Waste  Information  System  ("SWIS")  as an Unpermitted  Closed  Solid  Waste
Disposal  Site and SWIS  No. 19-AA-5545.  In 1984,  the State of California  Department  of Health
Services,  Toxic  Substances  Control  Division  concluded  that  the  clean-up  work  completed
effectively  mitigated  waste  constituents  to  proceed  with  the  Lewis  Homes  residential
development  project.  The  requirements  of the PCLUP  came into  effect  in 1988.  As  such,  the
project  site is subject  to State solid  waste regulations  that require  the PCLUP  before  any change
to the current  land use, construction,  or land preparation  can occur.

The Los Angeles  County  Department  of Public  Health,  Solid  Waste  Management  Program,  acts
as the  LEA  for  the  State  of California's  Department  of Resources  Recycling  and Recovery
("CalRecycle").  The  County  is  authorized  by  Division  30  of  the  Public  Resources  Code
("PRC"),  Section  43209  and 45000,  Title  14 and 27 of the California  Code  of Regulations  (14
CCR  & 27 CCR),  to enforce  applicable  solid  waste  regulations  and to ensure  solid  waste  sites
meet  the  state minimum  standards  within  the  County  of Los  Angeles.  As  such,  the  City  is
working  with  the LEA  to obtain  approval  of the PCLUP.

Construction  is  currently  at  the  90%  completion  stage.  Improvements  that  have  been
substantially  completed  include,  but are not limited  to, rough  grading,  drop inlet  for storm  water

planters,  planting  of  75  trees,  installation  of  the  prefabricated  education  center  and  the
restrooin/maintenance  building,  two  shade  structures,  a water  element  at the  playground,
installation  of multi-use  walking  and bicycle  patliways,  exercise  equipment  located  at various

and pathway  lighting.  Construction  of the project  will  resume  after  the County  approves  the
CPLUP.

  SUBJECT:  FUNDING  AGREEMENT  WITH  THE  LOS  ANGELES  COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN  TRANSPORTATION  AUTHORITY  FOR  MEASURE  R FUNDS  FOR
  THE  I-710/FIRESTONE  BOULEVARD  SOUTHBOUND  ON  RAMP  MODIFICATION
  PROJECT,  CITY  PROJECT  N0.  354 ST

  PURPOSE:  To  approve  a Funding  Agreement  with  the  Los  Angeles  County  Metropolitan
  Transportation  Authority  to accept  a grant in tlie amount  of $1,450,000  in Measure  R Funds  for
  the I-710/Firestone  Boulevard  Southbound  On Ramp  Modification  Project.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a,  Approving  Funding  Agreement  with  the Los Angeles  County  Metropolitan  Transportation
  Authority  ("Metro")  to accept  $1,450,000  in Measure  R Funds  for the I-710/Firestone
  Boulevard  Southbound  On Ramp  Modification  Project  ("On  Ramp  Project"),  City Project
  No. 354-ST;
  b.  Appropriating  $1,450,000  in Metro  Measure  R Funds  to the On Ramp  Project;  and
  c.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the Funding  Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The Funding  Agreement  allocates
  $1,450,000  in Measure  R Funds  ("Metro  Measure  R Funds")  to the On Ramp  Project  to fund
  $700,000  in design  costs and $750,000  in construction  costs.  All  of the grant funds  are required
  to be appropriated  to the On Ramp  Project.

  ANALYSIS:  The  I-710/Firestone  Boulevard  Southbound  On  Ramp  Modification  Project  is
  funded  by various  grant  funding  sources  some  of which  are from  Metro.  Under  the proposed
  Funding  Agreement,  the City  will  receive  a grant in the amount  of $1,450,000  in Metro  Measure
  R Funds  for the On Ramp  Project,  to fund  design  and construction.  The project  is in the design
  phase and fees have been incurred.  As such, Metro  has made the term of the agreement  retroactive
  to Januai'y  1, 2024, to pay for design  costs.

  BACKGROUND:  The On Ramp  Project  is a part of the Capital  Improvement  Program.  It is the
  second  phase  of a project  that is being  implemented  to improve  traffic  flow  and reduce  traffic
  congestion  on Firestone  Boulevard,  at the I-710  Freeway.  The  project  entails  re-aligning  and
  widening  the I-710  Freeway/Firestone  Boulevard  Southbound  on-ramp,  to align  to the widened

  73
 Firestone  Boulevard  Bridge,  at  the  Los  Angeles  River.  In  addition,  the  project  includes
improvements  on Firestone  Boulevard  from Rayo Avenue  to Garfield  Avenue  including  pedestrian
improvements,  updating  curb  ramps  to comply  with  American  with  Disability  Act,  sidewalks,
replacement  of the existing  median  island,  creation  of an aesthetic  theme  for the railings,  grinding
and overlaying  the existing  pavement  and traffic  signal  modifications  to accommodate  pedestrian
crossings.

The  design  of the project  is substantially  complete.  If Caltrans  approval  is received  timely,
construction  is planned  to start January  2025 and be completed  in 16 months.

PROJECTLOCATION:
The project is located at Firestone Boulevard in the City of South Gate, at the I-710 SoutbJbound On-
Ramp, between Rayo Avenue and Garfield Avenue.

This project limits  are From Rayo Avenue to Garfield  Avenue

NEXUS TO HIGHWAY OPERATION, DEFINITION/PROJECI' PURPOSE:
The purpose of this project is to alleviate a Non-Standard On-Ramp, enhance pedestrian  safety and
traffic flow and provide a dedicated through lane to the I-710 Freeway.

PROJECTBACKGROUND:
The proposed project improvements  include the reconstniction and Realignment of the I-710
Southbound On Ramp, from Rayo Avenue to the I-710 Northbound On Ramp at Garfield Avenue,
provide a median island at the Western approach (from Garfield Avenue to the I-710 Northbound  On
Ramp) and Firestone Boulevard improvements,  such as ADA ramps, High visibility crosswalks, new
sidewallc and asphalt pavement.

The City of South Gate in cooperation with the Califoriiia Department of Traiisportation (Caltrans) is

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  SEQUEL  CONTRACTORS,  INC.,  FOR  THE
CONSTRUCTION  OF THE  TWEEDY  MILE  COMPLETE  STREETS  PROJECT,  CITY
PROJECT  N0.  614-ST,  FEDERAL  PROJECT  NOS.  ATPL-5257  (039)

PURPOSE:  To  award  an  Agreement  to  Sequel  Contractors,  Inc.,  ("Sequel")  for  the
construction  of the Tweedy  Mile  Complete  Streets Project  ("Tweedy  Mile  Project").  The project
was competitively  bid and Sequel  submitted  the lowest  responsible  and responsive  bid.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:

  a.  Approving  an  Agreement  with  Sequel  Contractors,  Inc.  ("Agreement"),  for  the
  construction  of the Tweedy  Mile  Complete  Streets  Project,  City  Project  No.  614-ST,  in
  an amount  not to exceed  $7,745,175,  with  a construction  completion  schedule  of 180
  working  days; or

  b.  Approving  an  Agreement  with  Sequel  Contractors,  Inc.  ("Agreement"),  for  the
  construction  of the Tweedy  Mile  Complete  Streets  Project,  City  Project  No.  614-ST,  in
  an amount  not to exceed  $8,095,175,  with  a construction  completion  schedule  of 145
  working  days;

  c.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Agreement  in  a form  acceptable  to the  City
  Attorney;

  d.  Authorizing  the  City  Manager  to  approve  change  orders  administratively  up  to  a
  cumulative  amount  of $800,000  to be funded  with  project  contingency  funds,  to expedite
  approval  of change  order work  to avoid  construction  schedule  delays;

  e.  Authorizing  the  City  Manager  to  approve  pre-payments  of  construction  progress
  payments  for  the  construction  contract  to comply  with  state  legislation  that  requires
  payment  of invoices  within  30 days;

  f.  Declaring  the Tweedy  Mile  Complete  Streets  Project,  City  Project  No.  614-ST,  to be
  Categorically  Exempt  under  Title  14  of  the  California  Code  of  Regulations,  Section
  15301  of the California  Envirom'nental  Quality  Act ("CEQA");  and

  g.  Approving  the Notice  of Exemption  for the construction  of the Tweedy  Mile  Complete
  Streets  Project,  City  Project  No.  614-ST,  and directing  the City  Clerk  to file  it with  the
  Los Angeles  County  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.

ANALYSIS:  The proposed  Agreement  was procured  through  a competitive  bid process.  The
bid  documents  required  a Base Bid  and four  Additive  Alternate  Bids.  The lowest  bidder  was
required  to be deterinined  based on the lowest  total  amount  of the Base Bid  and four  Additive
Alternate  Bids.  Based  on  this  requirement,  Sequel  submitted  the  lowest  responsible  and
responsive  bid. The bid analysis  is included  in Attachment  "A."

The Tweedy  Mile  Business  District  is a thriving  comi'nunity  filled  with  businesses,  high volumes
of  pedestrians,  traffic  (26K  vehicles  per  day),  events  and  students  in  route  to  schools.
Construction  will  be disruptive  and  impact  these  activities.  The  schedule  stipulated  in the
proposed  contract  to complete  construction  is 180  working  days,  which  is approximately  9
months.  However,  contractors  were  requested  to also submit  bids  to complete  construction  in
145 working  days, for which  Sequel  submitted  a bid for an additional  $350,000.  The additional
amount  pays  for  costs  such as overtime,  that will  be incurred  due to the shorter  construction
schedule  and need for longer  workdays.  The City  Council  may award  a construction  contract  in

the amount  of either  $7,745,175 for a 180-working  day completion  schedule,  or $8,095,175,  for
a 145-working  day completion  schedule.

The  PROS  of  the  145-working  day  schedule  are  reducing  soft  costs  and  staff  time  by
approximately  $45,000;  reducing  construction  impacts;  reducing  potential  for safety  issues  due
to high  volumes  of pedestrian  activity  on a construction  zone;  reducing  potential  impacts  to
businesses;  and allowing  events such as the Tweedy  Mile  Fair to take place in 2025.  The CONS
are the additional  cost of $350,000  which  would  be paid from  the project  contingency  funds.

BACKGROUND:  The  Project  is a part  of the  Capital  Improvement  Program.  It proposes
safety,  traffic  circulation,  landscaping  and greening  and beautification  improvements  for Tweedy
Boulevard,  from  Dearborn  Avenue  to Dorothy  Avenue.  Project  improvements  provide  for

  safety,  enhanced  access  to public  transit  and bike  access,  addressing  deferred  maintenance,

 pavement,  sidewalks  and ADA  ramps;  enhanced  crosswalks  of which  four  will  have  flashing
 lights;  traffic  calming  measures  such  as curb  extension,  mid-block  bulbouts  and  enhanced
 signage;  replacing  street  furniture  and bus  stops;  landscaping,  sharrows,  and bike  racks.  The
 Project  will  not change  the traffic  signal  system  or signalizing  intersections  or eliminate  traffic
 lanes  - two  (2)  in  each  direction  will  remain  and will  not  install  dedicated  left  turn  lanes.
 Intersections  will  not be eliminated,  overhead  wiring  will  not be placed  underground,  and there
 are no plans to construction  road medians  or decorative  fountains.

  SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  GANNETT  FLEMING,  INC.,  FOR
  CONSTRUCTION  MANAGEMENT  AND  INSPECTION  SERVICES  FOR  THE
  TWEEDY  MILE  COMPLETE  STREETS  PROJECT,  CITY  PROJECT  N0. 614-ST,
  FEDERAL  PROJECT  NOS. ATPL-5257(039)

  PURPOSE:  To award a construction management services agreement for the Tweedy Mile
  Complete Streets Project ("Tweedy Mile Project"). The project is scheduled to start construction
  in August of 2024.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will consider:
  a.  Approving  an agreement with  Gannett Fleming,  Inc., to provide  Construction
  Management and Inspection Services ("Agreement")  for the construction of the Tweedy
  Mile Complete Streets Project, City Project No. 614-ST in an amount not-to-exceed
  $551,900;
  b.  Authorizing the City Manager to approve and execute amendments up to a cumulative
  amount of $100,000; and
  c.  Authorizing  the Mayor to execute the Agreement in a form acceptable to the City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL IMPACT:  There is no impact to the General Fund. The proposed agreement is in the
  amount of $551,900, and it will be funded with $177,060 from the Active Transportation
  Program Cycle 6 Grant Funds, $100,000 in Prop C Funds and $274,840 in SBI Funds.

  ANALYSIS:  The Tweedy Mile Project is in the Capital Iinprovement Program. Design has
  been completed, construction bids have been received, and start of construction is planned in
  August 2024. Construction may be completed in either 180 or 145 working days, as selected by
  the City Council. The Department of Public Works, Engineering Division, needs a construction
  management services consultant to oversee construction and inspection of the Tweedy  Mile
  Project. It requires hundreds of hours of effort to manage and inspect beyond the capacity of the
  Engineering Division.  A Request for Proposal ("RFP") was issued for construction management
  services, and Gannett Fleming, Inc. ("Gannett") was the highest ranked consultant.  The fee
  proposal received was negotiated from $624,964 to $551,900.  Fee adjustments were made to
  "right-size"  the fee to the needs of the Project.  The negotiated  fee proposal  of $551,900  is

  1
  132
 reasonable  and within  the acceptable  industry  standards  for construction  management  services.

The proposed  contract  amount  of $551,900  is the service  fee needed  to manage  construction  of
the project  with  a 180-working  day  completion  schedule.  If the  Council  elects  to award  a
construction  contract  based  on  a 145-day  completion  schedule,  then  the  proposed  contract
amount  may  be reduced  by  approximately  $37,000.  Cost  savings  are not  higher,  because
Gannett  would  incur  additional  costs such as due to longer  work  days and overtime.

BACKGROUND:  The  Project  is a part  of the Capital  Improvement  Program.  It proposes
safety,  traffic  circulation,  landscaping  and greening  and beautification  improvements  for Tweedy
Boulevard,  from  Dearborn  Avenue  to Dorothy  Avenue.  The vision  for Tweedy  Boulevard  is to
transform  the  corridor  into  an attractive  urban  environinent  with  a diverse  mix  use.  These
elements  have safety,  transportation,  beautification,  and quality  of life benefits.

A construction  agreement  is scheduled  to be awarded  by the City  Council  on July  9, 2024.  As
such, an agreement  for construction  management  and inspection  services  is now necessary.  Staff
recommends  awarding  an agreement  to Gannett  to manage  the construction  activities  under  the
Tweedy  Mile  Complete  Streets Project.

On April  15,  2024,  the RFP  was released  electronically  through  Planetbids,  published  on the
City's  website,  and  advertised  in  trade  jownals.  On  May  9, 2024,  six  (6)  proposals  from
perspective  consultants  were  submitted  to the City  Clerk's  Office.  A panel  comprised  of three
members  (City  Traffic  Engineer,  Principal  Engineer  and Senior  Engineer)  reviewed  and short-
listed  proposals  and  interviewed  the  top  three  consulting  firms.  This  qualification-based
selection  process  weighed  several  factors  such  as project  manager  and  team  qualifications,
experience  on similar  projects  and understanding  of technical  issues.  Based  on the criteria,
Garu'iett received  the highest  ranking  from  the panel.

Gannett  Fleming,  Inc., provides  the following  benefits  to the Project:

  *  Experienced  Consulting  Firm  - Gannett  is a civil  engineering  firm  establisl'ied  in 1915
  witl'i  several  hundred  employees.  Gannett  specializes  in the provision  of construction
  management  construction  inspection,  plan  review,  project  management,  and other  civil
  engineering  services.  Gannett  has successfully  delivered  similar  projects  for cities  such
  as South  Gate, Pico Rivera  and City  of Los Angeles.

  *  Qualified  Staff  - The selected  construction  manager  is a registered  Civil  Engineer  and
  Qualified  SWPPP  Practitioner.  He  has more  than  30 years  of  construction  industry
  experience  in  the  transportation  field  which  includes  work  associated  with  grade
  separations,  freeway  interchanges,  major  urban  arterial  improvements,  freeway
  replacement,  and capital  improvement  projects.  The construction  inspector  has 32 years
  of experience  as a Senior  Public  Works  Inspector  for  a wide  range  of projects,  with  a
  significant  amount  of  public  works  construction  observation  and  special  inspection
  experience.

  *  Negotiated  Competitive  Fees - Gannett  submitted  an original  fee proposal  of $624,964,
  which  was negotiated  to $551,900  and includes  a total of 2,138 hours  of service  for the 9-

construction  management,  inspection,  labor  compliance,  materials  testing  and  utility
coordination.

Construction  is scheduled  to begin  in August  2024.

PURPOSE:  To authorize  the City  Manager  to approve  a Purchase  Order  with  HERC  Rentals  for
temporary  HVAC  equipment  rentals.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to approve  a Purchase  Order  with  HERC  Rentals  to fund
  equipment  rentals  needed to operate the HVAC  systems  at City Hall,  the Police  Station  and
  Sports  Center  for up to a seven-month  period,  in an amount  not to exceed  $454,000;  and
  b.  Appropriating  $479,000  in General  Funds to fund the Purchase  Order  with  HERC  Rentals.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  An appropriation  of $479,000  in General  Funds  is needed  to fully  fund the
Purchase  Order  with  Hertz  Rentals.

ANALYSIS:  The  HVAC  systems  at City  Hall,  the Police  Station  and  Sports  Center  were
installed  over  30 years ago and are stressed  during  summer  months.  The  chiller  systems  at the
Police  Station  and Sports  Center  are in a condition  operationally  that are at times  inadequate  to
meet  demands  when  the outside  air temperature  exceeds  85 degrees  Fahrenheit.  City  Hall  air
handler  equipment  experiences  perfori'nance  reliability  issues  and tends  to fail  during  the same
period  and conditions.  The  Capital  Improvement  Program  has over  $6 Million  to make  major
repairs  and enhancements;  however,  work  will  be completed  in 2025.

In April  2024 as outside  temperatures  began to increase,  the Sports  Center  chiller  could no longer
meet the cooling  demands  of the ongoing  indoor  activities.  The Department  of Public  Works,  with
administrative  approval  ofthe  City Manager,  obtained  temporaiy  HVAC  equipment  rental  services
from  Herc Rentals  for required  systems  at City  Hall,  Police  Station,  and Sports  Center.  The total
estimated  budget  need for seven months of equipment  rentals  is $479,000. This provides $238,000
for the Police  Station,  $210,000 for the Sports Center,  $6,000 for the City Hall and a $25,000
contingency.

The City  has purchased  a chiller  for the Sports  Center  and Police  Station.  These will  be installed
as soon as possible  so as to eliminate  the need for equipment  rentals.
